questions.question: What is the name of the branch of river Godavari that joins the Bay of Bengal flowing through the Yanam enclave of the Union territory of Puducherry?

questions.question: As per National Multidimensional Poverty Index - Baseline Report, published by NITI Aayog in 2021, what percentage of population in urban areas is poor?
questions.solution:

__
 
• National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is an initiative by the Government of India to measure poverty in a comprehensive manner, taking into account various factors such as health, education, and living standards.
 
• The baseline report of MPI was published by NITI Aayog in 2021 and covers both rural and urban areas of the country.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, i.e., 8.81%, which represents the percentage of the population in urban areas who are poor according to the MPI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Multidimensional Poverty Index(MPI)

 
• It seeks to measure poverty across its multiple dimensions and in effect complements existing poverty statistics based on per capita consumption expenditure. 
 
• It has three equally weighted dimensions –health, education, and standard of living.
 
• These three dimensions are represented by 12 indicators: 
 
 
• Such as nutrition, school attendance, years of schooling, drinking water, sanitation, housing and bank accounts among others.
 
 
 
• According to Global MPI 2021:
 
 
• India’s rank is 66 out of 109 countries. 
 
 
 
• The National MPI is aimed at deconstructing the Global MPI and creating a globally aligned and yet customized India MPI for drawing up comprehensive Reform Action Plans with the larger goal of improving India’s position in the Global MPI rankings.

• Lowest (multidimensional poverty)

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Finance Commission of India?

A. The Finance Commission consist of a Chairman and four other members.

B. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are binding on the government and the government needs to grant funds according to the advice of the Commission,

C. Article 280 of the Indian Constitution talks about the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C only.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3 (A and C only).**
 
• The Finance Commission of India is a** Constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The Commission consists of a **Chairman and four other members appointed by the President of India.**
 
• The recommendations made by the **Finance Commission are advisory in nature and not binding on the government.**
 
• The government may accept or reject the recommendations.
 
• The Commission recommends the distribution of taxes between the Centre and the States, grants-in-aid to the States, and other fiscal matters.
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted every five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The President of India constitutes the Finance Commission every 5 years. 
 
• The finance commission is a constitutional body mandated by article 280 of the constitution. 
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are of an advisory nature only and therefore, not binding upon the government.
 
• It submits its report to the President of India.
 
• The first Finance Commission was constituted in 1951.
 
• The eligibility of members of the Finance Commission is determined by the Parliament of India. 
 
• Chairman of the Finance Commission submits his report to the President of India. 
 
• Composition: Chairman and 4 members.

questions.question: In which year did an American cytogeneticist named Joe Hin Tjio publish a research finding that defined 2n = 46 as the exact number of human chromosomes?
questions.solution:

__
 
• ** Joe Hin Tjio was an American cytogeneticist who published a research finding in the year 1956 that defined 2n = 46 as the exact number of human chromosomes.**
 
• Tjio's research finding was based on **his extensive experiments involving the counting of chromosomes in human cells using microscopy and other techniques.**
 
• The discovery of the exact number of **human chromosomes was a landmark achievement** in the field of genetics and had significant implications for the study of human diseases and genetic disorders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Cytogenetics **is the branch of genetics that studies the** structure and function of chromosomes and their relationship to cell behavior and inheritance.**
 
• The discovery of the exact number of human chromosomes was a **collaborative effort that involved several scientists, including Albert Levan, who worked with Tjio to confirm the finding.**
 
• (1950) is close to the actual year of Tjio's appointment at the University of** Lund in Sweden**, where he began his research on human chromosomes. Option 2 (1952) is also close to the actual year when** Tjio first observed and counted human chromosomes **under the microscope. However, neither of these options represents the year when Tjio published his research findings. Option 4 (1960) is too late as it comes after several other significant discoveries had already been made in the field of cytogenetics.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts added four new subjects (Article 39, 39A, 43A, 48A) in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the 42nd Amendment Act, of 1976.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The correct answer is option 1, i.e., the 42nd Amendment Act, of 1976 added four new subjects (Article 39, 39A, 43A, 48A) in the Directive Principles of State Policy.**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are the guidelines or principles given in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution to the government for the welfare of the people and the development of the country.**
 
• Article 39 deals with the principles of policy to be followed by the State in ensuring **social justice and the welfare of the people, while Article 39A deals with equal justice and free legal aid.**
 
 
 
• **Article 43A** ensures the participation of workers in the management of industries, and** Article 48A deals with the protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding forests and wildlife.**
 
• The Forty-first Amendment Act of the Constitution of India,1976, changed the age of retirement of the Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commissions from 60 to 62 years, by amending article 316(2) of the Constitution, while the** 40th Amendment Act, of 1976 amended the Constitution to extend the life of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from five to six years.**
 
• **The 39th Amendment Act, of 1975 **amended the Constitution to prevent any court from questioning the election of the Prime Minister and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Where does the lower salinity water rest with the higher salinity dense water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Above.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The lower salinity water rests above the higher salinity dense water due to the principle of density stratification.**
 
• This occurs because saltwater is **denser than freshwater, and as a result, the denser saltwater sinks below the less dense freshwater.**
 
• This phenomenon is important in **oceanography and marine biology, **as it affects the distribution of nutrients and organisms in the water column.
 
• Option 2, below, is incorrect as it goes **against the principle of density stratification.**
 
• Option 3, it combines, is also incorrect as the two types of water** do not mix but rather remain stratified.**
 
• Option 4, which is separate, is a vague statement that does not provide much information and can be considered incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Salinity is the measure of the concentration of dissolved salts in water.
 
• Density stratification refers to the layering of water based on differences in density, which can be caused by differences in temperature, salinity, and other factors.
 
• In oceanography, the layering of water based on density is called oceanic stratification, and it affects the ocean's circulation, climate, and ecology.
 
• Density stratification also plays a crucial role in the formation of ocean currents and the transport of heat and nutrients around the globe.

questions.question: The Vakataka dynasty was directly related to which Gupta emperor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra Gupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Vakataka dynasty ruled in central and southern India from the 3rd to 5th century CE.**
 
• **The Gupta dynasty** was a powerful and influential dynasty that ruled in northern India from the **4th to 6th century CE.**
 
• ** The Vakataka dynasty** was directly related to Chandra Gupta II, who was** a Gupta emperor.**
 
• **Chandra Gupta, I was the founder of the Gupta dynasty** and ruled from 320 to 335 CE, which was before the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• Shree Gupta, the grandfather of Chandra Gupta I, laid the foundation of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Samudra Gupta was a Gupta emperor who ruled from 335 to 375 CE, which was also before the Vakataka dynasty.
 
• **Option 4, Chandra Gupta II, is the correct answer as he was the Gupta emperor who was directly related to the Vakataka dynasty.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The Gupta Empire :

 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from the early 4th century CE to the late 6th century CE.
 
• At its zenith, from approximately 319 to 467 CE, it covered much of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This period is considered the Golden Age of India by historians.
 
• The ruling dynasty of the empire was founded by the king Sri Gupta; the most notable rulers of the dynasty were Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II alias Vikramaditya.

questions.question: Krishnadeva Raya composed a work on __________ in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**statecraft.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 1, i.e., statecraft.**
 
• Krishnadeva Raya was a ruler of the **Vijayanagara Empire, and he was known for his administrative skills and patronage of arts and literature.**
 
• Amuktamalyada is a Telugu composition that describes the story of the wedding of Lord Vishnu and Andal, a devotee of Vishnu. The work also includes advice on statecraft and governance.
 
• The work is considered a masterpiece of Telugu literature and is admired for its poetic beauty and insights into politics and ethics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vijayanagara Empire:

 
 
• Vijayanagara or “city of victory” was the name of both a city and an empire.
 
• The empire was founded in the fourteenth century (1336 AD) by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty.
 
• They made Hampi the capital city.
 
• In 1986, Hampi was declared a World Heritage site by UNESCO.

questions.question: __________ has become the 100th 'Har Ghar Jal' district in February 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chamba.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** 'Har Ghar Jal' is a government initiative aimed at providing piped water supply to every household in India by 2024.**
 
• ** Chamba, located in Himachal Pradesh, has become the 100th district to achieve the goal of providing a piped water supply to every household in February 2022.**
 
• Kachchh, located in Gujarat, is a district that has been severely affected by earthquakes and has faced water scarcity issues in the past. However, it is not the correct answer to the question.
 
• Mewat, located in Haryana, is a district that has been facing water scarcity and quality issues. However, it is not the correct answer to the question.
 
• Kurnool, located in Andhra Pradesh, is a district that has been facing drought and water scarcity issues. However, it is not the correct answer to the question.
 
• Hence, the statement "Chamba has become the 100th 'Har Ghar Jal' district in February 2022" is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jal Jeevan Mission (Har Ghar Nal se Jal)

 
 
• Launched in 2019.
 
• Aim: To provide every single rural household with functional household tap connections (FHTC) ‘Har Ghar Nal Se Jal’ by 2024.
 
• A decentralized approach is implemented at national, state, and district levels for specific needs and purposes (Targeted Area approach).
 
• The major role played by Paani Samitis and women in mobilizing the population.
 
• The Jal Jeevan Mission will be based on a community approach to water and will include extensive Information, Education, and communication as a key component of the mission

questions.question: What is known as aggregate monetary resources?

options.text: M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
M1 + Net time deposits of commercial banks
M3 + Total deposits with Post Office savings organisations (excluding National Savings Certificates)
Currency (notes plus coins) held by the public and demand deposits held by commercial banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** M1 + Net time deposits of commercial banks.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Poin__**

__
 
• **The correct answer to the given question is option 2, which is M1 (currency in circulation + demand deposits with commercial banks) + net time deposits of commercial banks.**
 
• Aggregate monetary resources refer to the** total amount of money available in an economy.**
 
• Option 2, which is **M1 (currency in circulation + demand deposits with commercial banks) + net time deposits of commercial banks**, is known as aggregate monetary resources.
 
• M1 + savings deposits with Post Office savings banks (option 1) is known as narrow money.
 
• M3 + total deposits with Post Office savings organizations (excluding National Savings Certificates) (option 3) is known as broad money.
 
• Currency (notes plus coins) held by the public and demand deposits held by commercial banks (option 4) are known as the monetary base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** M1 + savings deposits with Post Office savings banks is known as narrow money**.
 
• It only includes the most liquid forms of money, i.e., the currency in circulation and demand deposits with commercial banks, along with savings deposits with Post Office savings banks.
 
• It doesn't include time deposits or other forms of deposits with commercial banks.
 
• **M3 + total deposits with Post Office savings organizations (excluding National Savings Certificates) **is known as broad money.
 
• It includes all forms of deposits with commercial banks, Post Office savings organizations (excluding National Savings Certificates), and other financial institutions.
 
• It is a broader measure of money supply than M1 and M2.
 
• ** Currency (notes plus coins)** held by the public and demand deposits held by commercial banks is known as the monetary base.
 
• It is the total amount of currency in circulation and demand deposits held by commercial banks.
 
• It doesn't include time deposits or other forms of deposits with commercial banks.

questions.question: The colours of the squares used in a chessboard are ________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**white and black.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The colours of the squares used in a chessboard are white and black.**
 
• This is because the chessboard is designed to have a contrasting pattern of** light and dark squares to make it easier to distinguish between the pieces.**
 
• Red and black or white and green would not provide the necessary contrast for the chess pieces to stand out.
 
• White and red would also not work as it would be too bright and could cause eye strain.
 
• Option 1 is the correct answer as it accurately describes the colours used in a standard chessboard.
